mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand and economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of periods with sustained HOUST increases, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a quarter signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals a shift in demand towards consumption, which boosts consumer-oriented stocks and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month period signals deflationary pressures, which increases the real value of debt and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with sustained CPIAUCSL decreases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in GDP (GDPC1) exceeds the year-over-year change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2%, it signals real economic growth outpacing inflation, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: YoY GDPC1 growth > YoY CPIAUCSL growth by > 2%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
